system.summary: Lasry's 'TNA SP106-8' key (Jan 1646): a numerical homophonic alphabet of one- and two-digit values (up to four for a vowel) with a numbered word list from 100 up (100 all, 101 are, 108 and, 141 for, 173 I, 174 in, 176 ing ...), numbers separated by colons.
system.sibling_key: Same key, per Lasry's files, on R925 (ff. 238-240, a letter of the Queen, January 1646)
system.notes: Split on 14 Oct 2026 from the former hm1645, which joined six letters in four of Lasry's keys. Lasry's key file says there are no nulls; 11 low figures the key leaves without a value (21, 30, 42, 50, 16 ...) are left 'unknown' here. Other entries: hm1645 (TNA SP 106 key), sp106r787 (SP106-2), sp106r929 (SP106-5).

prior_solution.where: DECODE record files of R924 (George Lasry, 23 Oct 2020: reconstructed key, interlinear plaintext, dating notes)

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: apply_key.py (key applied group by group to the transcription and compared with Lasry's plaintext)

solution.what: Fetched the DECODE record page of R924 with the shared cookie; it links Pettersson's transcription, Lasry's reconstructed key 'TNA SP106-8' and his plaintext of ff. 235-236 and 238-240 (2020-10-23).

Re-fetched the record files and applied the key group by group to the 2012 groups of ff. 235-236 (apply_key.py): 1850 get a value; on the lines whose columns line up in Lasry's interlinear file (1604 keyed groups) every value equals his plaintext. 162 groups have no value in the key (58 distinct three-digit numbers, 11 low figures).

Split from the former combined target hm1645 under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): R924 is the only letter of the six in the SP106-8 key. Folder, profile, page and ledgers separated; the earlier step is kept as recorded.
Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): linked the DECODE record holding Pettersson's transcription and Lasry's plaintext; no local copy

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): Lasry's plaintext of R924 is on DECODE only (git-ignored copy in no checkout); nothing could be read. Relabelled decoded, not read; class already solved kept (Lasry's decipherment); fraction_read 0.9195 -> 0.

outcome.method_basis: The letter was taken from George Lasry's plaintext on the DECODE record (23 Oct 2020); his SP106-8 key, applied here only as a check, reproduces it.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Reading audit, 22 Oct 2026: the letter's text is not in the repository (Lasry's files were git-ignored and are in no checkout), so no tokens are in a document that reads here. The earlier 0.9195 (apply_key.py: 1850 of 2012 groups with a value in Lasry's key) is withdrawn as a reading figure.

gaps.item: three-digit word-list numbers not in Lasry's key (58 distinct, 85 tokens: 324, 428, 321, 532, 208, 797 ...)

gaps.item: low figures with no value in the key (11 distinct, 77 tokens: 21, 30, 42, 50, 16 ...)
gaps.detail: Lasry renders them '_'; dividers, nulls or values missing from his alphabet. Not settled here.

gaps.item: R924: Lasry's plaintext not in the repository
gaps.detail: his interlinear and plaintext files are on the DECODE record (reachable with the shared DECODE cookie (targets/bordeaux/decode/cookie.txt)); fetch them into decode/ (git-ignored, his work), grade them as sentences, and ask him whether a reading copy may be kept

outcome.notes: Nothing about the text is new: Lasry's decipherment on DECODE is the reading. DECODE's start date (26 June 1646) does not fit the letter's own 'Paris Jan'; queued as a correction. 22 Oct 2026, reading audit: no text of the letter is in the repository; decoded, not read. Class kept: Lasry's decipherment exists on DECODE (2020).

texts.label: R924, Paris, January 1646
texts.summary: A writer at Paris to Charles I against Sir H. Compton's journey and the treaty for Prince Charles's marriage with Portugal, on Montreuil's mission, the frost that stopped the river traffic, and levies of five or six thousand men to send over.
texts.note: Lasry's interlinear plaintext of R924 is on the DECODE record, behind its login, and was kept out of the repository as his work; no copy is in any checkout, so nothing of the letter can be read here (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026); fix: re-fetch it with the shared DECODE cookie (targets/bordeaux/decode/cookie.txt) and check it with apply_key.py.
